title: How does a river carry stones, sand and mud?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature

explain.say: A river is a conveyor belt for broken rock, carrying it from mountains to the sea. How it moves each piece depends on how big the piece is and how fast the water flows.

draw.text: How does a river carry stones, sand and mud?

explain.say: The biggest boulders are rolled and dragged along the riverbed, called traction. Usually this only happens in floods, when the water is deep, fast and powerful.
Pebbles and coarse sand bounce along the bed in little hops, called saltation. Fine silt and clay are light enough to float in the water, called suspension, which is what makes rivers look muddy.
Some minerals, like the calcium in limestone, dissolve completely and travel invisibly. When the river slows, it drops its load, biggest stones first and finest mud last.

faq.q: How does a river move boulders?
faq.a: Boulders are rolled and pushed along the bed, called traction. It takes fast, deep water, so big stones mostly move during floods.
asks: What is traction in a river?

faq.a: Saltation is when pebbles and sand grains bounce along a riverbed in short hops, lifted by the current and dropping back down.
asks: How do pebbles move in a river?

faq.a: Tiny particles of silt and clay are so light that moving water keeps them floating, called suspension. After heavy rain rivers carry much more, so they turn brown.
asks: What is suspension in a river?

faq.q: Where does a river drop its load?
faq.a: Wherever it slows down: on the inside of bends, in lakes, on floodplains during floods and at its mouth. The biggest stones drop first and the finest mud travels furthest.
As pebbles tumble and knock into each other and the bed, their sharp corners chip off. The further they travel, the smoother and rounder they get.
asks: Why are stones in rivers smooth?

facts: The Amazon carries roughly a billion tonnes of sediment into the Atlantic each year.
China's Yellow River is named after the yellow silt it carries.

quiz.say: How does fine mud travel in a river?
quiz.show: Fine mud travels in a river by…
quiz.why: Silt and clay particles are so tiny that the moving water keeps them suspended.

wrong.1: Rolling along the bed is how the biggest boulders move.
wrong.2: Fish do not carry the river's mud; the water does.
